Riff

Voice agent platform that generates deterministic FSM-based voice agents from plain English business descriptions.

https://github.com/davidbmar/riff  ·  private  ·  shipped

📄 Project documentation (80 docs) →

What it is

riff is a Python-based voice agent framework that combines Large Language Models for natural language understanding with declared Finite State Machines (YAML) for strict workflow enforcement. It allows developers to describe a business process in plain text, automatically generating a voice agent that handles phone conversations for tasks like scheduling, ordering, and intake. The system ensures reliability by using the LLM only for 'riffing' (language generation and slot extraction) while the FSM 'keeps the beat' (validating transitions, preventing hallucinations, and managing state).

Features

  • Generates voice agent flows from plain English business descriptions
  • Enforces deterministic state transitions via YAML-defined FSMs
  • Prevents LLM hallucinations through strict slot validation and guardrails
  • Supports multiple LLM backends including Gemini, Gemma, and Claude
  • Includes built-in web UI for real-time conversation inspection and debugging
  • Provides a self-improvement loop for tracking agent performance metrics

cd ~/src/riff

How it's built

Built in Python with a modular architecture separating deterministic logic from probabilistic LLM calls. Core components include a YAML-based flow loader, a pure-function state manager, guardrails layers, and adapters for STT/TTS/LLM providers (Gemini, Gemma, Claude). It uses a web server for API access and browser-based visualization, and includes a self-improvement loop for metric tracking.

How it runs

sequenceDiagram
    participant User as Caller
    participant STT as STT Service
    participant Server as riff Web Server
    participant FSM as State Manager
    participant LLM as LLM Adapter
    participant TTS as TTS Service
    User->>STT: Speaks audio
    STT->>Server: Sends transcribed text
    Server->>FSM: Get current state and constraints
    FSM->>Server: Return valid transitions and slots
    Server->>LLM: Request response with context
    LLM->>Server: Return generated text and extracted slots
    Server->>FSM: Validate slots and transition
    FSM->>Server: Confirm next state
    Server->>TTS: Synthesize response audio
    TTS->>User: Plays audio response

How to apply & reuse

Use riff to rapidly prototype and deploy voice agents for customer service, appointment booking, or order taking without hard-coding dialogue trees. Describe the business logic in English, generate the flow via API, and integrate the resulting voice endpoint into telephony systems. It is suitable for developers needing high-reliability voice interfaces who want to avoid the unpredictability of pure-LLM agents.
